Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

Key findings: 50-year-old male with T2DM, hypertension, overweight status, presenting with 4–5 days of dry cough (occasional purulent sputum), rhinorrhoea, sore throat, subjective fever/rigors, shortness of breath, myalgias, and brief diarrhoea. No chest pain. No in-person exam or vitals available.

Working diagnosis: Acute viral upper respiratory infection / influenza-like illness (including possible COVID-19).

Supporting rationale: Acute onset, typical viral prodrome (cough, runny nose, sore throat, myalgias, subjective fever), self-limited gastrointestinal symptoms; DDx model rates likelihood high.

Considerations:  
• Community-acquired pneumonia – medium likelihood due to purulent sputum, dyspnoea, diabetic risk; plan for watch-and-wait with delayed antibiotics (Amoxicillin Rx provided) and safety-netting.  
• Acute bronchitis – medium likelihood, overlapping features.  
• ACE-inhibitor–induced cough and congestive heart failure exacerbation considered low likelihood.

Management:  
• Rest, adequate oral fluids.  
• Paracetamol for fever/discomfort.  
• Delayed prescription: Amoxicillin 1 tablet TID for 5 days (exact strength not documented) to start if no improvement in 24–48 h.  
• Advice to seek urgent care if worsening shortness of breath, persistent fever, chest pain, or no improvement by next week.  
• Chronic disease optimisation: schedule HbA1c, BP review, weight management support.  
• Smoking cessation encouragement; alcohol moderation discussed.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

1. Acute viral upper respiratory infection / influenza-like illness (incl. COVID-19) – High likelihood: Abrupt onset of cough, rhinorrhoea, sore throat, myalgias, subjective fever over 4–5 days matches classic viral picture.  
2. Community-acquired pneumonia – Medium likelihood: Purulent sputum, feverishness, increasing dyspnoea in a diabetic smoker raise concern; no objective signs yet.  
3. Acute bronchitis – Medium likelihood: Sub-acute cough post-URTI with mild systemic features, often self-limiting.
